common_name: Blue Moon Torenia (Semi-Trailing Powder-Blue Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Set out transplants once all frost danger has passed and nights stay reliably warm; this Danziger-bred selection is semi-trailing, so it fills baskets and container edges faster than upright torenia types.

directions: Grow in evenly moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where Blue Moon spills gently over container rims and basket edges rather than mounding upright like older torenia strains. Its powder-blue tubular flowers carry a deeper indigo throat and continue opening from a self-cleaning habit, so spent blooms drop cleanly without deadheading. It tolerates heat and humidity better than many shade annuals but will stall and bleach out in strong direct sun, so keep it out of afternoon exposure in warm climates. A light monthly feeding keeps the semi-trailing stems full through a long spring-to-frost bloom season.

common_name: Indigo Moon Torenia (Semi-Trailing Deep Purple-Blue Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Transplant into containers or beds after frost danger has passed; Indigo Moon's semi-trailing stems benefit from a hanging basket or raised planter where the flowers can be viewed from below.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, since this Moon series selection carries some of the darkest, most saturated indigo-blue coloring available in the Torenia hybrida line. The semi-trailing habit is well suited to hanging baskets and window boxes, where the deep-colored blooms show clearly against pale companion plants. Keep the shallow root zone from drying out during summer heat, as torenia stops flowering quickly under drought stress and is slower than most annuals to recover. No deadheading is needed since the plant sheds spent flowers on its own through a continuous spring-to-frost bloom cycle.

common_name: Magenta Moon Torenia (Semi-Trailing Vivid Magenta Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Set transplants out once nights are reliably warm after last frost; Magenta Moon's bright color and semi-trailing form make it a strong focal plant in mixed shade containers.

directions: Set plants into moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where the vivid magenta blooms hold their color best out of direct midday sun. Magenta Moon's semi-trailing stems spread gently over the edges of pots and baskets rather than growing upright, giving mixed shade containers a softer, cascading profile. The plant flowers continuously without deadheading and shows good tolerance of summer heat and humidity for a shade annual, though it still needs steady moisture to avoid wilting. Pair it with pale or white-flowered companions to make the intense magenta stand out in low-light plantings.

common_name: Purple Moon Torenia (Semi-Trailing Dark Violet Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all danger of frost has passed into shaded beds or containers; Purple Moon's brownish-red throat and yellow tongue read best up close in shaded seating areas or raised planters.

directions: Grow in evenly moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where Purple Moon's dark violet-blue lobes and contrasting brownish-red throat catch the eye against greener shade foliage. The semi-trailing habit fills hanging baskets and container edges without becoming rangy, and spent flowers drop cleanly so deadheading isn't necessary. It flowers from spring through frost with good resilience to summer heat and humidity, provided the soil never dries out completely. Feed lightly on a monthly schedule to keep the long bloom season going strong.

common_name: White Moon Torenia (Semi-Trailing White Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Transplant into shaded beds or containers once frost danger has passed; White Moon's pale flowers brighten deep-shade plantings and show up well in evening light.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where White Moon's pale flowers with their small yellow throat marking lighten up the darkest corners of a shade garden. The semi-trailing stems drape softly over pot rims and basket edges, making it useful for softening the front of mixed shade container plantings. It blooms continuously from spring to frost without deadheading and tolerates summer heat reasonably well for a torenia, as long as soil moisture stays consistent. Use it to visually brighten deep shade beds where darker-flowered companions can otherwise look muddy.

common_name: Yellow Moon Torenia (Semi-Trailing Yellow Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Set out transplants after all frost danger has passed; Yellow Moon is one of the few true yellow-flowered torenia selections and stands out strongly against darker Moon series colors in mixed baskets.

directions: Grow in evenly moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, since Yellow Moon's clear yellow blooms are uncommon among wishbone flowers and add a warm accent color to shaded plantings dominated by blues and violets. The semi-trailing habit is well suited to hanging baskets, window boxes, and the edges of raised containers. It flowers without interruption from spring through frost and needs no deadheading, though consistent soil moisture is essential since torenia's shallow roots dry out quickly in summer heat. Combine it with blue- or purple-flowered Moon series selections for strong color contrast in shaded container displays.

common_name: Clown Violet Torenia (Compact Violet Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or set out transplants once frost danger has passed, into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Clown Violet's trailing tendency makes it a good choice for hanging baskets as well as beds.

directions: Plant in partial to full shade in consistently moist, well-drained, fertile soil, where Clown Violet's rich violet tubular flowers with bright yellow throats and pale calyces stand out against the surrounding foliage of most shade plantings. Compared with the more upright Clown Burgundy and Clown Rose already grown in this dataset, Clown Violet has a somewhat looser, semi-trailing habit that lets it spill nicely over the edge of a hanging basket or raised bed. It flowers continuously from late spring through frost without deadheading and holds up well through humid summer heat, though it will bleach and stop blooming in direct sun. Keep the soil evenly damp, since torenia's shallow roots dry out and stall flowering faster than most bedding annuals.

common_name: Clown White Torenia (Compact White Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or set transplants out once frost danger has passed, into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Clown White's pale blooms brighten dim corners better than the darker Clown series colors.

directions: Set plants into consistently moist, well-drained, fertile soil in partial to full shade, spacing them roughly 8-10 inches apart for a tidy, well-branched mass. Clown White carries clear white tubular flowers accented by a small yellow throat spot, giving it more visual lift than the burgundy, rose, and violet Clown series colors in deep-shade plantings where light-colored flowers read best. It stays compact and well-branched without pinching, flowering continuously from late spring through frost with no deadheading required. Keep soil evenly moist through summer heat, since torenia's shallow root system stalls flowering quickly once it dries out.
